verdict.rationale: Grafana's own SLO feature (Grafana Cloud) lets SREs create SLIs and SLOs that define an acceptable service level and how to react when it is not met. That covers the SLO-definition core of the story. However, the evidence never explicitly mentions error budgets or burn-rate alerting, and Grafana's general alerting is a separate feature that cannot stand in for SLO-specific burn-rate alerts. missing for 10: documented error-budget tracking, documented burn-rate alert rules (e.g., multi-window/multi-burn-rate), independent or hands-on corroboration of the SLO feature.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can define SLOs with error budgets and burn-rate alerts

citations.quote: By creating SLIs (Service Level Indicators) and SLOs, you define what an acceptable level of service is and how to react if you are not providing the expected level of service.
Grafana SLO (Service Level Objective) provides a framework for measuring the quality of service you provide to users.
With Grafana SLO, you can create metrics to measure the quality of the service you provide users.
